name: Bright Olive
lede: Bright Olive is a vivid yellow-green, one of several near-identical clusters the 2010 xkcd color survey recorded independently under different names.

sections.title: Four names, one cluster
sections.body:
The xkcd survey logged this exact shade, or something within about two CIEDE2000 units of it, under at least three other labels besides Bright Olive: Gross Green, Pea, and Sick Green [1]. That scatter is typical of the survey's method; thousands of people typing free-text names for the same swatch rarely agree on one word, and "olive" itself reads very differently to different eyes [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[avocado]], [[acid-green]], [[mustard-green]] and [[fibrous-green]], at 2.9, 3.7, 3.8 and 4.5 ΔE [1]. Siblings are [[olive]], [[kelly-green|Kelly green]], [[chartreuse]], and [[army-green|Army Green]], all crowded into the same yellow-green corner [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, has no painting where this vivid yellow-green covers five percent or more of the canvas [2]. A green this saturated and this light together is rare in aged, varnished oil paint; most archive greens of comparable hue sit darker or duller [2].
